The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. - **Opening:** White answered my C4 with the mirror point F4. The line I chose (C4, G6, D5 hane, solid C5/C6/C7, E7/F7/G7 on top, D3/E3/E2 at the bottom) went well. At move 33 the counting script projected me at 47–49 points, and Black needs 45 to win.
- **The mistake:** my top-right group was completely walled in, and its only room for eyes was the small corner area G8–J9. I spent moves 37 and 41 on edge points worth 1–2 each (F1, A8) instead of H8 to secure eyes there. This is the same mistake my notes have flagged about a dozen times.
- **What White did:** White played G9 and H9 inside the corner, then pushed at J7, which left the corner in seki (neither side can capture the other). Then White deliberately gave up three stones at G8. Capturing them left me a bent three, a three-point eye shape where White can take the key point, and White took it with G9, so the group was dead. I passed hoping the engine would score the group as alive, but it counted it dead.
